title: Spiral Order Traversal
hints: Maintain four boundaries and shrink one after each side of the spiral.
Right along the top, down the right, left along the bottom, up the left.
Guard the bottom and left passes so a single remaining row or column isn't repeated.
jsBridge: Shrinking four boundaries (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) is the same as in JS. Swift traps on any off-by-one index where JS returns `undefined`, so boundary mistakes show up immediately.

compass.q: An off-by-one in JS gives `undefined` in the output. In Swift it crashes. Which is easier to debug?
Single-row and single-column matrices: which loop condition breaks first?
Boundary shrinking vs a direction vector with a `visited` grid: which is simpler to get right?
Where do spiral or zigzag traversals appear (image processing, game boards)?
